items.detail: **Meta and Tesla** report after Wednesday's close, the week's big test for the Nasdaq after last week's **4.5%** drop on AI-spending fears.
items.why: Bigger AI spending plans without matching revenue would deepen the selloff; reassuring guidance could spark a relief rally.

items.detail: The Fed has gone quiet before its Oct. 27–28 meeting, so Friday's **flash PMIs** and consumer inflation expectations are the week's only notable US data.
items.why: Hot price readings would revive rate-hike bets and push the 10-year yield further above 5%.

items.detail: Chip-equipment maker **Lam Research** also reports Wednesday after the close, with the **S&P 500** starting the week at 7,659.
items.why: Chipmakers led last week's losses, so Lam's China and memory-chip outlook will show whether that damage spreads.

items.detail: The **Bank of Korea** decides rates Thursday, and 19 of 20 economists polled expect it to hold at **3.00%** after hikes in July and August.
items.why: A surprise hike would add to pressure on a Kospi already below 6,000; a hold that hints at November keeps chip stocks cautious.

items.detail: Indian markets close Tuesday for Dussehra, and the **₹30,213 crore Jio Platforms IPO** takes bids Wednesday to Friday, with the Nifty starting at 23,146.
items.why: India's biggest-ever IPO could pull cash away from other stocks, while crude prices and foreign selling remain the main risks.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** starts the week in a correction, about **11%** below its August record, with Friday's flash PMIs the main scheduled test.
items.why: Small companies with floating-rate debt suffer most if hot price data keeps yields above 5%.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** starts near **$81,500** and is holding $80,000 support, with Wednesday's Meta and Tesla results the main risk event in a week with no Fed speakers.
items.why: Another tech selloff or rising yields could break $80,000, especially after ETF outflows of about $228 million last week.

items.detail: **Ether** starts near **$2,409**, and the key thing to watch is whether US spot ether ETF outflows continue after about $320 million left last week.
items.why: Continued outflows with no upgrade this week leave $2,400 at risk; a halt would steady prices.

items.detail: Solana's **Alpenglow** upgrade goes live on mainnet Wednesday at about 14:50 UTC, aiming to cut transaction finality to roughly 150 milliseconds, with **SOL** near $104.
items.why: A smooth launch could stop the ETF outflows; problems or another delay could push SOL below $100.

items.detail: **Gold** starts near **$4,180**, and Friday's flash PMIs and inflation expectations are the week's main test, with oil near $110.
items.why: Hot price data would lift yields and the dollar, hurting gold; a soft reading would bring back inflation-hedge buying.

crossCuttingTheme: With the Fed silent, Wednesday's Meta, Tesla and Lam results test whether heavy AI spending can be justified, while oil near $110 keeps yields above 5%, setting the tone for chips, small caps, crypto and gold.
